title: Angular's TypeScript 7-Powered Compiler Enters Beta with Rust-Based Preprocessor
gist: Angular is rewriting its compiler's analysis stage in Rust (the Angular Preprocessor, ngp, built on VoidZero's Oxc) because TypeScript 7's Go rewrite removed the Transformer API its ngc compiler relied on; early benchmarks show 2–3x faster cold builds and halved memory, with production adoption gated on TypeScript 7.1 in an Angular 22 minor.

insights.claim: Microsoft's Go-based TypeScript 7.0 removed the ts.Transformer API that Angular's ahead-of-time compiler (ngc) depends on to turn decorators like @Component into runtime instructions, forcing Angular to decouple compilation from TypeScript's APIs.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Native-language rewrites of core JS tooling break downstream ecosystem APIs, forcing costly framework re-architecture.
insights.locator: The existing compiler, ngc, wraps tsc

insights.claim: The Go port of TypeScript offers no cross-language equivalent of the Transformer API, and crossing the JS/Go boundary at every file would be prohibitive for performance.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Language-boundary costs push the JS toolchain further toward native (Rust/Go) implementations end to end.
insights.locator: The Go port offers no cross-language equivalent

insights.claim: Angular's new preprocessor ngp is built on Oxc, VoidZero's Rust toolchain that already powers Vite, and the team frames it as a partial rewrite rather than a fresh start.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: VoidZero's Rust toolchain is consolidating as shared infrastructure across major JS frameworks.

insights.claim: ngp runs in three stages: a parallel Rust/Oxc frontend discovers Angular declarations, the existing TypeScript template compiler emits a runtime file and a Type Check Block, and a downstream tool (tsgo, tsrs, esbuild or Rolldown) handles type-checking and JS emission.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Decoupled, pluggable compiler stages make bundler/typechecker choice interchangeable — a competitive opening for Rust-native tools.

insights.claim: The bulk of Angular's ngp landed on 8 October in one commit of more than 370,000 lines, around 56,000 of them Rust.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Scale of the rewrite signals strong Google commitment to Angular's toolchain modernization.
insights.locator: The bulk of ngp landed on 8 October

insights.claim: Independent benchmarks of the ngp beta across projects of 15 to 1,714 components showed 2x–3x faster cold builds, with memory on the largest project falling from 2.8 GB to 1.4 GB; ngp plus tsrs and Rolldown was the fastest pipeline, tsgo plus esbuild only marginally slower.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Build-time and memory halving reduces CI compute costs for large enterprise Angular estates.
insights.locator: Cédric Exbrayat of Ninja Squad benchmarked

insights.claim: A prototype vite-plugin-ngp reached first page in 10.5 seconds versus 17.4 for ng serve on a 252-component codebase, applied template edits in 112 ms instead of a 2.6 s full reload, and on a 5,000-component app cut startup to 1.6 s from 28.4 s.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Vite-based dev servers could displace Angular's own CLI dev loop, strengthening Vite's dominance.
insights.quote: is a prototype on a prototype

insights.claim: VoidZero's experimental Oxc Angular compiler, which reported roughly 97% improvement on narrower workloads, is now described as actively seeking maintainers, while the Angular team's ngp becomes the official path after collaboration between the two groups.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Official framework teams tend to absorb community/vendor experiments; standalone forks lose maintainers.
insights.locator: VoidZero's own experimental Oxc Angular compiler

insights.claim: Angular expects ngp adoption to land in a minor release of Angular 22 once TypeScript 7.1 restores the compiler API; until then production builds should remain on ngc, and older apps must first upgrade to v20 or later.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Enterprise Angular migration timelines are gated on TypeScript 7.1 — watch its GA as the trigger.
